text:
rachel: quick idea: piggyback owner tokens onto existing lease heartbeats to avoid extra RPCs and keep affinity.

dong: that saves calls but couples ownership to liveness. what about nodes that are quiet for a while?

rachel: plan: workers include X-Owner-Token and X-Epoch in heartbeat; control-plane issues tokens. heartbeat every 700ms for hot prefixes; stale after 2s.

maya: how does this affect zero-copy shared buffers? we previously relied on refcounts across processes.

rachel: tokens authorize handoffs; buffers remain refcounted. release emits invalidation marker + refcount--. actual free occurs when refs==0 and epoch is stale.

omar: mixed-version rollout? old nodes ignore headers. avoid double-ownership by falling back to a proxy slow-path that gets ephemeral token via CAS. proxy limited concurrency and emits metrics.

sanjay: ops playbook: detect leaks by querying owner_registry, check last_renew_ts, snapshot refcounts, and CAS reclaim if safe. add dry-run reclaim endpoint.

rachel: eviction tweak: if owner recently renewed -> demote rather than free; if owner stale -> tombstone then free after refcount zero or TTL (default 30s).

maya: metrics: owner_header_hit_ratio, lease_renew_rate, orphaned_ref_count, proxy_fallback_total, handoff_latency_p95.

omar: tests: concurrent release+read, double-acquire races, mixed-version proxy stress. add fuzzing with varied delays.

deploy-bot: Canary window: Sun 03:00-07:00 UTC. Tag "owner-heartbeat-canary-1".

rachel: will open RFC follow-up with diagrams, token format (compact 16-byte), test matrix, and rollout checklist. thanks all.
